Commentary.Commentary: We are back. The players are out in the middle. Ibrahim Zadran and Rahmanullah Gurbaz to open for Afghanistan. Aryan Dutt to bowl first. A short leg in place, now the player has been moved to mid-wicket.
...THE CHASE...

Right then! Not a big total on the board. This looks like an easy win for Afghanistan but the Dutch bowlers are in red-hot form. They have to bowl really tight in the first 10 overs, 2-3 wickets at the top is what they needed. Stay tuned.

Mohammad Nabi is in for a chat. He says the first 10 overs weren't good but they did well later on and they bowled in the right areas and did really well. Adds he has good experience and he tries to use it.

Afghanistan were coming in four spinners and all of them were tidy with their spells. Mohammad Nabi ended with three while Noor Ahmad came in late to claim two wickets. Afghanistan were on top in the fielding department as well which gave them four wickets.

A clinical performance by the Afghan bowlers. They couldn't have asked for a better performance than this. More than their bowling, it was a poor display of batting from the Dutch. Netherlands love to put runs on the board and it worked their way on the toss. They lost Wesley Barresi but the stand between Max O'Dowd and Colin Ackermann flourished. The seamers though were poor with their line and were put off dearly. However, poor communication and poor cricket saw Afghanistan lose four of their top five wickets through run outs. Very rarely you see it. Wickets kept on falling as the pressure got too big on them and have fallen well below par here.

UP GOES THE FINGER! Paul van Meekeren reviews but it is in hope! OUT! THREE REDS! That is the end of it. This lands outside off and spins back in. Paul van Meekeren looks to sweep but misses and is hit on the pad. Netherlands are BOWLED OUT FOR 179!

Afghanistan (PLAYING XI) - Rahmanullah Gurbaz, Ibrahim Zadran, Rahmat Shah, Hashmatullah Shahidi (C), Azmatullah Omarzai, Ikram Alikhil (WK), Mohammad Nabi, Rashid Khan, Mujeeb Ur Rahman, Fazalhaq Farooqi, Noor Ahmad (IN FOR Naveen-ul-Haq).

Hashmatullah Shahidi says he would have batted first too. He feels the wicket might take turn. Adds the toss does not matter and they are looking forward to this game. Informs they are going in with four spinners.
Scott Edwards says they want to bat, it has worked well for them and they hope to defend the runs they put on the board. Informs they have one change.
TOSS - Netherlands have won the toss and ELECTED TO BAT!

We say this is going to be an exciting clash because that is the brand of cricket the two have played. They are the giant killers in this World Cup. The Dutch have managed to beat South Africa and Sri Lanka whereas, Afghanistan are well and truly in the race for qualification. However, they will need to win this game, it is not going to be easy because Netherlands have proven to be a challenge for many. The Afghans though are still favourites and especially in Lucknow where the wickets will suit their bowling.

It is time for yet another game from this year's World Cup and it is a clash between two teams which have done exceedingly well so far. Yes, they are 6th and 8th on the points table but they have performed a lot better than one must have expected from them. Afghanistan are taking on Netherlands and this is well and truly an important clash more so for the former. This promises to be an exciting clash. Stay tuned for the toss and teams.
... MATCH DAY ...

Netherlands and Afghanistan will face each other in a must-win match at the Ekanna Cricket Stadium in Lucknow. Talking about the Netherlands, it will be a tough challenge for them as they suffered a massive batting collapse against Australia. They did bounce back and won the following game against Bangladesh. As such, the top four of the Netherlands' batting lineup need to find their form and deliver some crucial partnerships. They cannot continue to rely on the lower order to rescue them time and again. Vikramjit Singh and Max O'Dowd must put up a gritty stand here and play out at least the first powerplay to give them a good headstart. The middle order is quite strong, with the likes of Colin Ackerman, skipper Scott Edwards, and Bas de Leede. In their game against Bangladesh, it was their skipper Scott Edwards who played a steady knock of 68 runs when their team was falling apart and made the side reach a par total of 229 runs. Then their bowling unit performed well and bundled the Bangladesh side for 142 runs to register a comfortable victory. Sybrand Engelbrecht is another talent to watch out for, as he has been excellent in the past few games. On the other hand, Afghanistan are having a great World Cup, beating England, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka. Their batting has been brilliant so far. After their defeat against the Kiwis, their batters did excellent. While chasing 283 against Pakistan, their openers struck a 130-run partnership. They won the game with 8 wickets to spare. In the very next match against Sri Lanka, Gurbaz was dismissed without scoring, but Rahmat Shah, Shahidi, and Omarzai all scored half-centuries and won the game with seven wickets in their kitty. Their bowling unit has done well, and the team will expect a similar performance from them in this game as well. This pitch in Lucknow has something for the bowlers, and both sides will look to take maximum advantage of it. While Afghanistan may have a slight edge based on their current form, the contest could still be closely fought and go either way.
